decisions.reason: As a training programme closely tied to the installed base, it is inexpensive to maintain and supports equipment sales and customer lock-in, so the option value of keeping it open remains high.
This accessory builds on the firm's core machines and likely has modest carrying costs, so even with limited visibility the firm would usually keep it unless demand proved clearly weak.

Because hybrid additive post-processing is distant from the firm's established offer and likely requires more specialized development and market building, weak early evidence would make abandonment the more likely real-options choice.

A high-speed CNC milling machine is close to the firm's core capabilities and strategic direction, so despite higher resource needs the firm is likely to preserve this option while exploiting its existing know-how and service network.

An automatic tool change system strongly complements the firm's productivity-oriented equipment portfolio and can be maintained at relatively low risk, which favors retaining it as part of the core solution set.
